owner_posts.post_text:
ANTICIPATORY BAIL IN FRAUD AND FORGERY CASE

Present case is Anticipatory Bail Application filed apprehending arrest in FIR for offences u/s. 420, 465, 467, 468, 479 r/w. 34 of IPC. Applicant introduced accused no. 2 land broker to first informant. It is alleged that Applicant was one of the beneficiaries under the aforesaid land transaction. Further, documentation prepared and facilitated turned out to be forged and fabricated since informant was unable to mutate their names in the land revenue records pertains to said land parcel as the land purchased by them was tribal land hence there was embargo. 

Court observed that, there is unexplained delay of 4-5 years in filing FIR. Further most of allegations are against Accused no. 2. Rights of parties were governed by Agreements and other documents. The applicant’s role was limited to introduce parties and facilitating preliminary steps which does not amount to offence u/s. 420 IPC. Prima facie the dispute between parties is of a civil nature coupled with absence of essential ingredients of the alleged Sections. It is not the prosecution case that Applicant participated in forgery. The allegations appeared to be related to a failed investment and land acquisition transactions and subsequent grievance is predominantly of a civil nature. Thus custodial interrogation of applicant neither warranted nor necessary in facts especially when accused no.2 already enlarged on bail. Anticipatory Bail granted to applicant.

Bombay High Cout

UNILATERAL CONVEYANCE OF PLOT

THE CASE:
Competent authority has granted certificate in favour of Housing Society for unilateral conveyance deed. The Developer - Plaintiff has questioned its validity before City Civil Court. The stay was granted in the said suit and hence the present appellant has challenged the same in appeal.

ARGUMENTS:
It was contented by the Developer that, in the agreement for sale executed with flat purchaser it was agreed to create lease interest in respect of portion of larger plot and not whole plot.

The question falls for consideration was “whether competent authority granting unilateral execution of conveyance deed in respect of larger plot was in accordance with agreements executed?

As per section 10 and 11 of MOFA Act Competent Authority is to perform duty and obligation which Promoter is to perform under law i.e. to convey title and execute documents. The entitlement of exact quantification of FSI on the plot cannot be gone into in proceedings. 

CONCLUSION:
Court determined that, agreement format was prescribed for first time in 1986, therefore question of conveyance as per agreement does not arise. It is observed that, constructed area of building is disproportionate to the area of building agreed to convey. Therefore, Court confirmed the Competent Authority’s order of unilateral conveyance of larger plot. 

Bombay High Court

RIGOROUS IMPRISONMENT IN CHEQUE BOUNCING CASE

On request of accused complainant paid Rs.2,50,000/- to accused as a hand-loan on 28.12.2004. Accused issued post-dated cheque. Complainant deposited the cheque in the Bank which was dishonoured on account of insufficient funds. Hence after issue of notice complainant filed a complaint u/s. 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.	

During trial accused pleaded not guilty however he admitted to have issued cheque. He contended that it was issued on 01.02.2004 and the complainant altered it to 31.12.2004. The cheque dated 01.02.2004, therefore, barred by limitation.

Trial court recorded conviction u/s. 138 of the N.I. Act and sentenced the accused to undergo imprisonment for three months along with compensation.

Appellate court confirmed conviction of trial court but set aside the rigorous imprisonment of 3 months without assigning any reason. Accused was not shown as handicapped nor he was above 55 years of age. Therefore, leniency shown by appellate court was not justified hence judgement set aside.

Bombay High Court

RECOURSE WHEN POLICE REFUSE TO REGISTER FIR

Section 175(3) of Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita - BNSS (section 156(3) of CRPC) is used when police refuse to register the FIR. Protest Petition can be filed by Victim when police submit negative report refusing to register FIR. It is filed by the Victim when Police submit negative report for closure of case. Protest Petition aims to ensure justice by issuing directions to Police to register FIR upon hearing.

The Protest Petition usually filed before Police register FIR. The Magistrate has power under BNSS section to hold investigation or preliminary inquiry when report u/s. 176 of BNSS is received. 

Protest Petition is treated as complaint, it allows the victim to lead the evidence so that Magistrate can take cognizance and order investigation.

This provision is very important as it safeguard the justice to the victim and increase Police accountability for FIR registration and investigation.

This mechanism administer justice where police fail to act or where police ignore Magistrate’s order. Hence it provides recourse for inaction.

KNOW WHETHER TRANSFERRING MINOR’S PROPERTY IS AN OFFENCE


In the case before hand complainant is the owner of the piece of land and he is in possession. He came to know that, father transferred minor’s (his) property to society without obtaining permission from competent court and repurchase it back from society. Therefore, criminal complaint was filed alleging that, accused has committed criminal breach of trust and prepared false documents and executed will deed. 

It is alleged that, property transferred favouring society was without legal necessity. Further society was controlled by accused only and society later on transferred back the said land in favour of accused. Hence there was dishonest intention since inception. It is submitted that, alienation of minor’s property is voidable at his instance. FIR cumulatively shows that all the accused conspired together to cheat minor to cause wrongful gain and wrongful loss to minor. 

Accused advocate submitted that, if we consider all the allegations of FIR, still it does not disclose any material showing forgery or cheating. FIR filed 35 later years after attaining majority by minor and after 48 years of executing documents against 78 years old father and 74 years mother and to apply pressure and harass them. Therefore, FIR held liable to be quashed.

Bombay High Court

featured_reviews.name: Hussain Lakhani
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Lifesaver in My Legal Battle
I am beyond grateful to Adv. Geetanjali for her exceptional legal expertise, relentless dedication, and unwavering support in clearing my name from a false case. She successfully secured a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the police station and obtained my exit permit from the FRRO, allowing me to return to the USA. Without her tireless efforts, I would have remained stuck in a legal nightmare that disrupted my life for months.

Unmatched Legal Expertise & Commitment
My ordeal began when I overstayed my visa by just one day. As a result, I found myself trapped for nine months, struggling with unresponsive authorities at the FRRO. Despite repeated visits, I was left waiting in the reception area every day for over a month, was not allowed to meet the officer handling my case.

Feeling lost in an unfamiliar legal system, I searched for a lawyer on Google and found Adv. Geetanjali, who had a five-star rating. From our very first meeting, I knew she had the expertise and experience to handle my case. She listened patiently, understood my situation as a foreigner unfamiliar with local laws, and immediately took action.

When we visited the FRRO together, for the first time, I was allowed to go beyond the reception area and meet the officer in charge of my case. That’s when we discovered a case had been mistakenly registered against me due to mistaken identity.

Adv. Geetanjali meticulously researched my case, filed a petition in the Bombay High Court, and fought relentlessly for four months. Despite six different court dates and repeated delays due to holidays, she successfully got the case dismissed. The next major challenge was securing the NOC from the police station—for my exit process.

Securing the NOC
Obtaining the NOC should have been straightforward, but due to bureaucratic inefficiencies and election-related delays, it turned into a three-month ordeal.

Shockingly, the FRRO had to use POSTAL SERVICE instead of emails as per their rules to to request NOC from the police station—email was not an option! This outdated rule caused unnecessary delays. Since many Police Officers were unavailable due to elections, Adv. Geetanjali and I made 15 trips between the FRRO and the police station before finally securing the NOC.

Exit Permit from FRRO
With the NOC in hand, the next step was paying the overstay fine—but another frustrating obstacle awaited.

I was shocked to learn that the FRRO only accepts payments via Indian-issued bank cards—cash, foreign cards were not accepted. This made things incredibly difficult for foreigners who had no access to Indian bank accounts. Fortunately, I was able to use my significant other’s card.

Even after completing the payment, the FRRO unexpectedly asked me to resubmit my application and reupload all my court documents for the THIRD TIME. This forced me to go through the entire process a third time.

Finally, after 9 months I received my exit permit, allowing me to fly back to the USA and leave this nightmare behind.

Beyond Just Legal Help – A True Support System
What sets Adv. Geetanjali apart is not just her legal brilliance but also her compassion and dedication. She was always available to answer my concerns, offer reassurance, and guide me through this incredibly frustrating and emotional journey.

She understood the mental and emotional toll this ordeal took on me and always ensured that I remained hopeful and strong.

A True Champion of Justice
Because of Adv. Geetanjali’s relentless hard work, legal expertise, and dedication, I am now free from the false allegations that once threatened my future. I was able to reclaim my life and return to the USA—all thanks to her unwavering commitment.

If you are facing legal challenges, need expert guidance, or require assistance with police clearances, FRRO procedures, or exit permits, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND Adv. Geetanjali. She is not just a lawyer—she is a true lifesaver!

Thank you, Adv. Geetanjali, for giving me back my freedom and peace of mind!

featured_reviews.name: Bhagyasree Barman
featured_reviews.review_text:
My mother, sister and I were separated from my father for 12years. He lived and worked alone in USA while supporting us in India. It was difficult emotionally to live separately and laborious for my father to work alone. After many hardships, Advocate Geetanjali Naidu has reunited us with my father!

Adv.Geetanjali was recommend to my father by our US Attorney in Feb 2021,  my father had applied for Green Card visa twice for me and my mother in 2013 and 2018 but both the time my visa got rejected, while all this while I was minor, so I thought I will get it soon,  as my father had twice submitted all my files and my mother’s file in USA, but 2nd time in Jan 2021 when my mother’s  GC visa got approved and my GC visa got rejected by the Mumbai US Consulate, I was heartbroken and lost all hopes as I had aged out now (as I waited for 12 long years) and there was no call from the US Consulate for review, didn’t know how long the waiting period was for and when they will call me. Because of my visa rejection my mother and my younger sister couldn’t go to USA as we all wanted to go together and live with my father.

Adv.Geetanjali  is a specialist in immigration cases and expert in her feild! When my father spoke with her about my case, we were worried about the whole process- whether my age would be a factor, if I would receive a GC visa at all or not? But she explained the process to us very clearly and in an understandable way! This put our worries to rest completely when we saw how invested she was in our case! She gave me hope with her calm and confident manner and I was assured that I would get my visa very soon! She was with me in every step of the whole process, she was very generous and made it clear that I could call her for help which I am very grateful for! My family and I never met Adv.Geetanjali in real life, not even on video call or zoom! All our consultations were done over the phone, online and through emails! Which I think is incredible-to never even have to be face to face but still give such attention to every single detail- this quality of-course makes her work absolutely impeccable as compared to others!
She is very professional  and precise with all information sharing and phone consultations, I have never seen anyone who is as efficient as she is in her work!

Adv.Geetanjali drafted all documents and reconfirmed with us for all corrections, then officially submitted.The whole process took approximately  1 month, after submission, in just SIX days later,I had my visa in my hand!! No Queires from the Consulate, and I had never dreamed it would all be done so fast!! I am so excited to start a new life with my family in the USA finally!

Adv.Geetanjali is a huge reason that I have an opportunity for a better life now! My family and I are so grateful and appreciative of all her hard work and efforts!!

I've learnt that processes such as this should always be done with an expert lawyer’s advice and guidance such as her to get the best and fast results! I feel that if I had known her in 2016, our family would have been together a long time ago! But anyway we are together now. And I would highly recommend Adv.Geetanjali as an expert immigration lawyer in India for Consular Processing or any matter to anyone who is facing problems in  submission, interview or Consular Processing or has been unfairly rejected. She also gave me excellent advice even after I received the GC visa on what to expect in post landing procedures in USA! All over, Im so grateful to her and I have come out from this experience more knowledgeable because of her!
---B.Barman- Kolkata, India
